scenes.head: The Medicare Part D late enrollment penalty
scenes.big: What it is and how to avoid it
scenes.say: The Medicare Part D late enrollment penalty. What it is, and how to avoid it.

scenes.head: When does it start?
bullets: After you are first eligible, you go 63 days or more in a row
Without Part D or other creditable drug coverage
scenes.say: A penalty may apply if, after you are first eligible, you go 63 days or more in a row without Part D, or other creditable prescription drug coverage.

scenes.head: How it is calculated
bullets: times each full month you went without coverage
scenes.say: The penalty is one percent of the national base premium, for each full month you went without coverage. The 2026 base premium is thirty eight dollars and ninety nine cents.

scenes.head: It can last
bullets: Added to your monthly plan premium
Generally lasts as long as you have Medicare drug coverage, even if you switch plans
scenes.say: The amount is added to your monthly plan premium, and it generally lasts as long as you have Medicare drug coverage, even if you switch plans.

scenes.head: How to avoid it
bullets: Enroll when you are first eligible
Do not let a gap reach 63 days
Ask about Extra Help, which removes the penalty
scenes.say: To avoid it, enroll when you are first eligible. Keep your creditable coverage notices. Do not let a gap reach sixty three days. And ask about Extra Help, because people who receive it do not pay the penalty.

scenes.head: Questions about your situation?
scenes.big: Fill out the form at honorbrook-insurance.com
scenes.say: Questions about your situation? Fill out the short form at honorbrook insurance dot com, or call five seven one, three five four, zero one four six. A licensed agent will reach out.
